# Antigravity account setup

Read this reference when selecting antigravity_cli or diagnosing its account/tool
configuration. KH runs the owner's installed, signed-in agy CLI. This account
route does not need a Google API key. It does not establish the paid plan's name
or guarantee that every model is available to that account.

## Local account and executable

Follow Google's [installation and authentication instructions](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/cli/install/).
Run agy --version, open agy and complete its native account login. Inspect
agy models before recording the actual owner-selected model. AGY_CLI_PATH can
name an explicit executable; otherwise KH uses agy from PATH.
KH neither installs this CLI nor logs in on the owner's behalf.

The native settings file ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json must not select
modelProvider: gemini for this account route. KH refuses that API-key provider
setting instead of changing global authentication. The adapter withholds API-key
and provider-override environment variables from this subprocess.

## Role configuration

Choose runtime/model/effort through the existing setup command while idle:

```text
/kh-setup-models --set builder=antigravity_cli:MODEL:EFFORT
/kh-setup-models --set builder=antigravity_cli:MODEL:EFFORT --apply
/kh-models --doctor
/kh-start --dry-run "Exact accepted task request"
```

MODEL and EFFORT are placeholders for the owner's actual available choice.
Preview writes nothing. Applying records the selected profile in .kh/models.json
and .kh/routing.json without invoking a provider. Other roles and profile limits
are preserved. Saved choices also apply to mapped standalone calls such as
/kh-prompt --agent builder; that single phase is not full guarded acceptance.
Each needed role must be configured independently.

The adapter requires an explicit tool list and harness_engineering: [].
It refuses tools: null. Safe builder tools are read, grep, find, ls, edit and
write; actual writes remain limited to project source scope and phase evidence.
A file-only builder can edit Swift source while the controller runs configured
quality commands. Review roles keep source writes empty but need a write tool
when their phase requires an evidence file.

KH installs a temporary native PreToolUse hook in the role's isolated workspace.
It validates hook discovery and session/invocation attestations, denies unknown
tools and controller/protected-path writes, preserves prior hooks and removes
its temporary additions after confirmed completion. This is a tool/path gate,
not an OS or network sandbox for any granted shell process. Native Antigravity
approval remains authoritative; KH does not pass auto_approve or bypass denial.
See [headless behavior](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless/) and
the [transport contract](delegation.md#antigravity-account-transport).

## Native tests and compatibility

Add bash only when the owner requires execution inside the role and has
configured its exact quality captures. Do not grant blanket Bash access to
work around a host denial. The [test-command reference](test-command-permissions.md)
defines literal grants and the two process-local database override forms.
Declaring required_test_commands or approving a plan grants no tool or permission.
Known conflicts fail before building; external permission remains unverified
until a real tool receipt.

Model choices stay fixed for a running invocation. Persist defaults after the
writer ends or choose --use before a later run. No model switch expands scope,
checks, native permissions or limits. See [model choice](model-choice.md).

## Evidence and limits

The [configuration reference](config.md#antigravity-account-transport) and
[delegation contract](delegation.md#antigravity-account-transport) define result
grace, process cleanup, final evidence sealing and normalized usage.
Transport success still requires the ordinary scope, checks and independent
review gates. Tokens are normalized without adding thinking twice; unreported
dollars remain unknown, never measured free use. Cost is informational.
